summary: Memos is a self-hosted knowledge base application designed for capturing and organising notes. It stores data locally in a SQLite database file, keeping your information self-contained. The project is released under the MIT licence.
goodFor: It suits individuals looking for a lightweight, single-tenant personal wiki or scratchpad that runs without a complex external database dependency.
watchOut: SQLite may become a bottleneck or present backup challenges if you scale to heavy concurrent usage or very large volumes of data. It also overlaps with numerous established note-taking tools, so check if specific features you need are present.
deployNotes: You will typically run it via Docker, ensuring you mount a persistent volume for the SQLite database file to avoid data loss on container recreation. A reverse proxy is usually required in front of the container to handle TLS termination.
